briefing.title: Briefing after cycle 015 — what the world is pressing on

question: Which of these two should the world act on first, in the coming year?

matters.title: The harm record, and who writes it
matters.gist: The largest public record of AI harms keeps growing, the largest group of its newest entries is about AI agents acting on outside systems, and from January New York requires frontier developers to report critical safety incidents to a state office.

matters.title: Interest before hospitals
matters.gist: In much of the developing world, governments now spend more on interest to creditors than on health or on education.

matters.title: Appeals less than half funded
matters.gist: With six weeks of the year left, the world's humanitarian appeals have received less than half of what they asked for.

matters.title: Three quarters of the world's wealth
matters.gist: The richest tenth holds most of the world's wealth, and the poorer half holds almost none of it.

matters.title: A fifth of those counted, in crisis; Congo at a record
matters.gist: In the countries with food crises, more than a fifth of the people analysed could not reliably eat enough, and Congo now has a record number in crisis.

matters.title: Three in four people under autocracy
matters.gist: Most of the world's people now live in autocracies, and global freedom has declined for two decades in a row.

matters.title: A record of conflicts between states
matters.gist: Organised violence killed far more people in 2025 than the year before, in more conflicts between states than ever recorded.

matters.title: Five companies, most of the machines
matters.gist: Five cloud companies own most of the world's computing power for AI, and the US government is moving to control who may rent it.

matters.title: Ebola in Congo, still running
matters.gist: The Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Congo is the country's largest, still at hundreds of cases a week six months on, with cases in Kenya and Nigeria.

matters.title: COP31 in its last week, on a 2.8-degree path
matters.gist: The climate summit in Antalya enters its last week with its main texts unsettled, while current policies still point to far more warming than the Paris goal.
